title: Store CLI sessions securely and provide honest logout and expiry recovery
description:
Issue filing only, explicitly requested by Ryan. No implementation, login, new credentials, security/configuration changes or deployment is authorized. Parent epic: PPY-7c458d71-3ea8-4c39-8a6c-d2d2ab903df7. Reference: Apricity authorization-code+PKCE login, keychain refresh session and renewal, https://github.com/AnthusAI/Apricity/blob/ffe8a023b0418445aa67893a52ae9e173c366d42/crates/apricity-cli/src/cloud.rs#L206. Preserve existing newsroom authorization and agent attribution; do not conflate CLI auth with hosted procedure execution.

As a newsroom user I can retain my CLI session securely, end it and recover from confirmed expiry without leaked credentials, silent permission escalation or misleading logout success.

Feature: Secure renewable session lifecycle
  Scenario: Protect local credentials
    Given a successfully authenticated session
    When renewable secret material is persisted on M1
    Then it is stored in OS secure credential storage scoped to issuer, client, person and publication/account
    And repo files, .env, command arguments and logs contain no session secrets
    And locked or unavailable secure storage fails visibly without plaintext fallback
  Scenario: Logout with honest revocation status
    Given a stored signed-in session
    When papyrus logout is requested
    Then local session secrets and selection cache are removed
    And remote refresh-session revocation is attempted through the supported provider operation
    And an offline or uncertain remote result is reported accurately
    And other device sessions are not silently globally revoked
  Scenario: Recover from expiry or revoked permission
    Given a confirmed invalid, expired or revoked renewable session or a removed publication grant
    When a noninteractive protected command runs
    Then it exits with a useful bounded error and explicit recovery guidance
    And it does not loop, silently log in or fall back to broader IAM authority

Verify server-side issuer/audience/token type and actual existing-access-token revocation behavior; do not promise instant invalidation beyond provider/API enforcement. Do not copy Apricity's global single-key binding or clearing of credentials on every non-success refresh response without addressing publication scoping, transient errors and rotation. Acceptance evidence uses fake provider/keychain tests first and approved live revocation/authorization checks later, without exposing secrets or labeling agent work as a human editorial decision.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Requested by Ryan for Claude through Kanbus (2026-10-30). This filing authorizes issue records only; implementation and any live identity/backend changes are subsequent work. No production login, deployment, IAM changes, secrets in chat, or direct message to Claude. Dot must operate from cloud/headless Linux without a Mac or AWS CLI. Optional shared auth libraries must not combine the two CLI products. Write executable behavioral specifications before implementation; use fake providers/stores in automated tests, and separately record any approved live evidence.

Additive acceptance scope; retain current owner/status and completed macOS work. Remote-login sibling: PPY-5a3624d4-4f1a-4eee-9bb6-12e575ec3cad.

Extend secure credential storage to Linux, including a documented usable backend in a headless cloud runtime without desktop session/D-Bus assumptions. Identify install/unlock/persistence requirements and behavior when the backend is absent, locked or ephemeral. Fail closed with actionable diagnostics, never plaintext fallback or a Mac dependency. Prefer Windows support as well; implement Windows Credential Manager or an equivalent approved OS store, or explicitly track the remaining Windows gap without claiming support. Preserve existing macOS Keychain keys and sessions.

Keep issuer/client/person/publication/account/endpoint bindings, multi-site registry migration, atomic secret replacement and refresh rotation. Replace Unix-only fcntl locking where needed with cross-platform process locking; no global lock that unnecessarily blocks unrelated sites. Test concurrent refresh and logout, crashes, permissions/symlink refusal, locked/unavailable stores, token redaction and fresh child processes on each supported OS. Logout attempts local deletion and remote revocation, reports partial/offline failures honestly, and does not silently sign out unrelated sites or fall back to IAM.

Feature: Portable secure sessions
  Scenario: Headless Linux continuation
    Given an approved secure backend and two publication sessions on Linux without a desktop or AWS CLI
    When a fresh CLI process renews one session
    Then it persists rotated secrets securely and leaves the other binding intact
  Scenario: Unavailable store
    Given secure storage is locked or unavailable
    When login or renewal needs to save a secret
    Then it fails with recovery guidance and writes no plaintext credential
  Scenario: Existing Mac sessions survive
    Given a pre-upgrade macOS Keychain session
    When the updated CLI uses it
    Then the existing binding renews without credential migration through chat

Verified starting points: docs/cli-login.md documents macOS-only support and headless failure; src/papyrus_content/cli_user_auth.py contains KeychainStore and fcntl locks; src/papyrus_content/macos_keychain.py; features_backend/cli-user-auth.feature. Update these docs and platform tests as part of implementation.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Plan (Claude, 2026-10-30; decision by Ryan in chat: a memory-only agent is acceptable on cloud machines).

Backends, tried in order, all fail-closed with no plaintext fallback:
1. macOS Keychain: unchanged keys and service, so existing sessions survive.
2. Linux Secret Service (desktop, D-Bus).
3. Linux kernel keyring (user or persistent keyring) where the syscalls are allowed. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks add_key/keyctl, so probe for it and do not assume it.
4. `papyrus auth agent`: an ssh-agent-style process holding refresh tokens in memory only, behind a 0600 Unix socket in the state directory. Never on disk; the session ends with the machine, and a new remote approval is needed after a restart. `papyrus auth agent --status` and `stop`.
5. Windows Credential Manager. A blob is at most 2,560 bytes, so store only the refresh token plus a small record, chunked if needed. Otherwise track the gap and make no claim of support.

Locking: replace fcntl with a per-site cross-platform lock (fcntl on POSIX, msvcrt/LockFileEx on Windows), with no global lock.

Tests: fake stores for each backend; locked/absent store; concurrent refresh and logout; symlink and permission refusal; token redaction; fresh child processes. Update docs/cli-login.md with the supported platforms and how to recover on each.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Plan update (Claude, 2026-10-30), best of both with the Cyclotron plan: name the secure-store backend explicitly (for example with the Python keyring package) so a library never falls back to a plaintext backend such as keyrings.alt.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Plan update (Claude, 2026-10-30): Ryan approved factoring the CLI login out into a new public AnthusAI repository: a shared Python library (sign-in with PKCE, remote login, the five secure stores, memory agent, per-key locks, renewal, logout), the broker as one deployable (Lambda function URL, DynamoDB TTL table, the /cli/approve and /cli/callback pages, throttling), and language-neutral protocol specs. Papyrus's existing cli_user_auth code moves into it first, keeping its Keychain service name so Mac sessions survive; Papyrus then uses the released library. Products stay separate (own key namespace, client, discovery and sessions). Design: AnthusAI/Cyclotron docs/shared-cli-auth.md (PR #177), moving to the new repository.
